newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Products Outlook - Midco gasoline riding high.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Products Outlook - Midco gasoline riding high.

text.p: Spot Midwest gasoline is expected to steal the products limelight again this week, with short covering keeping differentials firm amid tight supplies and delays for Gulf Coast shipments on the Explorer Pipeline.

U.S. Gulf Coast product prices were seen holding their recent ranges, though prompt reformulated gasolines may see further gains in differentials after the strength seen late last week, while New York Harbor levels were seen steady.
Group Three unleaded differentials jumped Monday morning, adding to the three-cent rally there last week, as buyers snapped up barrels to cover commitments for delivery by May 20 and May 31.

Unleaded differentials rose a half cent over NYMEX gasoline to between 7.00 cents and 7.50 cents a gallon by midday Monday, as the market digested news of a fire Friday at Ashland's 70,000 barrel per day Minnesota refinery.
"A lot of people were counting on barrels, but they won't make it in time," one Group trader said, referring to a continuing seven-to-ten-day shipment delay by the Explorer.

"There's no chance of 14th cycle stuff hitting the Midwest by the end of the month so I expect the delays to create another bubble" in differentials this week, the trader said, as players attempt to lay hands on scarce material.

Although buying interest was not as hot in the less-vulnerable Chicago market, prompt differentials widened a half cent during the week with offers about 2.75 cents over the June print by late Friday.

Midwest traders were spurred into a buying mode by an Explorer announcement last Wednesday forbidding transfer of line space between the three delivert cycles in May because of full-capacity flow in the 575,000 barrel per day pipeline.
Explorer typically allows clients to nominate shipments for specific cycles, with the option of switching their reservation of line space to other cycles during the same month.
U.S. Gulf players called for a mostly sideways market for the coming week, though some recent refinery problems should keep reformulated A1 gasoline differentials firm.

Prompt reformulated A1 differentials jumped nearly one cent last week, with barrels offered about 0.15 cent under the NYMEX. The shutdown of Phillips' Sweeny Texas refinery on May 12 and the fire at Citgo's Corpus Christi alkylation unit led to the bullish move, traders said.
Phillips said Monday that the Sweeny facility should be back to normal operations between the May 21-25.
New York Harbor gasoline markets were expected to remain well-supplied in the near term despite what some traders characterized as relatively modest gasoline imports over the next several days.
Few European sellers appeared willing to meet buyers' levels on the East Coast, where bids appeared fairly thin, traders said.

In addition, the restart of Tosco's Trainer refinery last week kept many players a little jittery, since that facilty is expected to produce about 110,000 barrels per day of gasoline when running at full capacity.
"We don't know exactly what effect that will have on the spot market," one East Coast player said. "But I think that amount of finished gasoline put into this market would be felt."
Tosco said last week it expected Trainer to operate near its capacity early this week, though many traders said that appeared to be an optimistic projection.
